Strategy’s shareholders are getting antsy watching other investment sectors completely out perform Bitcoin especially as of recent and might want their money back.

Saylor has completely dropped the ball for the past 5 years on his Bitcoin purchases. And It’s not that Bitcoin hasn’t seen decent gains - it’s that Saylor’s buying strategy isn’t profiting from those gains. His average is 75k and he’s has been buying since 2021 when in late 2022 we dropped to 15k.

Sucks $BTC is dropping but it doesn’t change my overall view.

We’ve had almost every single historical indicator that’s flashed green for a start of a new bull market flash green on HTF.

We’re following the typical “crash before/during midterm elections”

Stocks are incredibly strong despite what retail thinks.

Interest rates + inflation should drop considering consumer spending has been up for several months while company performance has also been up.

Wages are finally starting to bridge the gap between cost of living.

Democrats own the house and senate while Trump remains President means the government will stay stagnate meaning companies can take on risk knowing nothing will pass/change.

This drop seems a little funny considering nothing on HTF pointed towards - no bear divs, no strong bear PA, no reversal patterns. We dumped due to midterms + binance hack IMO.

I still own my $BTC spot position. It doesn’t matter if $BTC is 80k or 60k today because I don’t plan to sell it for at least a year to take advantage of capital gains taxes + I have my conviction to hold for the upcoming bull run.

For those of you who really believe it’s “over”. We had a world wide pandemic where everyone thought the human race was going to go extinct and stocks pumped 115% off lows with $BTC running from 3k to 20k+ in a single year.

My best piece of advice is to DCA these levels and be thankful you have another opportunity to buy low.

opus_audit.actionable_recommendation_de: Nicht als Richtungs-, Makro- oder Altcoin-Signalquelle nutzen. Directional Theses, kurzfristige Shorts und Zyklus-Kalender-Prognosen höchstens als Sentiment-Indikator betrachten. Allein explizite BTC-TRADE_CALLs mit konkretem Entry/Target eignen sich als Kandidaten-Filter für den Horizont 7–14 T, stets mit eigenem Stop (orientiert am Median-MAE von etwa 4–5 % bzw. 1–1,5× ATR) und eigener fundamentaler Gegenprüfung (Liquidität, ETF-Flows, On-Chain). Vor jeder Gewichtung sollte ein Out-of-Sample-Paper-Tracking über mindestens 30 neue TRADE_CALLs laufen, mit Zielkriterium p < 0,05 nach Kosten. Parallel sollte die Vollständigkeit des Datensatzes geprüft werden (Tweet-Zähler im Profil vs. 742 erfasste Tweets), um Deletion-Bias einzugrenzen.
